cases.name: lone-field-is-scalar
cases.notes: The README §7 example: one line-form occurrence → card scalar, block_id of the paragraph (b_1: the heading is b_0).

cases.name: bracketed-square-and-paren
cases.notes: §3.2 form 1: value runs to the closer, trimmed.
cases.source:
# T

See [element:: quick silver] in the text (state:: liquid metal).

cases.name: bracketed-mixed-openers
cases.notes: §3.2: the opener and closer need not match.
cases.source:
# T

A [k:: v) and (k2:: w] here.

cases.name: multi-word-value-and-trimming
cases.notes: §3.2: values are trimmed of spaces and tabs on both sides.

known_for::    tria prima   

comp::	salt	

[sp::   spaced  ] and (tab::	t	)

cases.name: key-case-preserved
cases.notes: §3.2: the `i` flag widens the match; the key is stored as written, so these are four distinct scalar keys.

cases.name: repeats-are-list-in-order
cases.notes: §3.2: three occurrences → card list, ord in document order, duplicate values kept.
cases.source:
job:: janitor

job:: salesman

job:: janitor

cases.name: bracketed-before-line-form-within-a-block
cases.notes: §3.2 scan order inside one block: all bracketed matches first, then line-form — so `bracket` is ord 0 and `line` ord 1 although it comes first in the bytes.
cases.source:
# T

k:: line
see [k:: bracket] too

cases.name: booleans-exact-lowercase-only
cases.notes: §3.2 coercion: only exact `true`/`false` → bool; other casings are strings.
cases.source:
# T

done:: true

open:: false

t:: True

f:: FALSE

cases.name: numeric-coercion-table
cases.notes: §3.2 / §8: JavaScript `Number()` — decimal, leading/trailing dot, exponent, sign, and unsigned hex/octal/binary.

cases.name: non-numeric-strings
cases.notes: §3.2: `Infinity` is not finite; underscores, units, a bare prefix, a signed hex, separators and inner spaces are strings.
cases.source:

a:: Infinity
b:: NaN
c:: 1_000
d:: 12px
e:: 0x
f:: -0x10
g:: 1,000
h:: 1 000

cases.name: empty-value-is-empty-string
cases.notes: §3.2: an empty captured value is the empty string (type string, val_text "").

cases.name: range-not-detected-inline
cases.notes: §3.2 / §8: inline values are never range-detected — plain strings, no val_json.

cases.name: field-in-code-fence-ignored
cases.notes: §3.2: code_fence blocks are skipped entirely.

cases.name: field-in-inline-code-ignored
cases.notes: §3.2: code spans are masked before scanning; the bracketed field outside code survives.
cases.source:
# T

Use `key:: value` or `[k:: v]` here, but (real:: yes).

cases.name: fence-inside-list-item-masked
cases.notes: §3.2 masking inside a container's raw: the list's and the items' raws contain the fences (indented ≤ 3), so mask_code blanks them (backtick and tilde alike) and nothing matches; the code_fence children are skipped.
cases.source:
# T

- item
  ```
  key:: v
  [k:: v]
  ```
- other
  ~~~
  key:: w
  ~~~

cases.name: backtick-fence-with-backtick-in-info-is-not-a-fence
cases.notes: §3.2: a backtick fence whose info string contains a backtick is not a fence (CommonMark) — for the parser too, so these lines are paragraph text and the continuation-line field counts per container level.

cases.name: fenced-code-inside-blockquote-masked-as-a-code-span
cases.notes: §3.2 (as built): the blockquote's raw has `> ` before the fence markers, so mask_code's FENCE rule does not fire — but its code-SPAN rule does: the three backticks on line 1 are closed by exactly three on line 3, blanking everything between, so nothing matches at the quote level either; the nested code_fence child is skipped.

cases.name: continuation-line-field-in-list-item-anchored-to-the-item
cases.notes: §3.2 / §8 Containers (1.1): the list scans its own text (the item blanked), so only the item's `raw` matches → one scalar row anchored to the item.

cases.name: bracketed-field-in-blockquote-anchored-to-the-paragraph
cases.notes: §3.2 Containers (1.1): the blockquote's own text is its `> ` prefix; the nested paragraph holds the bracketed field → one scalar row anchored to the paragraph.

cases.name: marker-line-field-anchored-to-the-item
cases.notes: §3.2 line form (1.1): a list marker (`- `, `1. `) may precede the key, so `- job:: x` and `1. num:: y` are fields of their items; the lists' own text is blank.

cases.name: task-marker-line-field
cases.notes: §3.2 line form (1.1): a task checkbox after the marker is admitted, so `- [ ] due:: friday` is a field of the task block; `[ ]` is not a bracketed field (`[` must be followed by a key).

cases.name: ordered-and-bullet-marker-line-fields
cases.notes: §3.2 line form (1.1): `1.`, `1)` and `*` markers; three occurrences of one key across three lists → card list, ord in document order, each anchored to its item.
cases.source:
# T

1. key:: v

1) key:: w

* key:: z

cases.name: nested-list-item-marker-line-field
cases.notes: §3.2 (1.1): a field on a nested item's marker line belongs to that inner item (the outer item's own text is `- a` plus indentation).

cases.name: marker-line-bracketed-field
cases.notes: §3.2 (1.1): a bracketed field on a marker line is one occurrence for the item; the line form does not also match (`see` is not followed by `::`).

cases.name: loose-list-own-text-is-whitespace-yields-no-list-row
cases.notes: §3.2 (1.1): a loose list's own text between its items is only line endings, so the list contributes nothing; the two items' marker-line fields are list rows ord 0 and 1.

cases.name: continuation-line-field-with-children-anchored-to-the-paragraph
cases.notes: §3.2 Containers (1.1): an item with children keeps no text of its own (`spec/format` §3 single-paragraph fold does not apply), so the continuation line lives in the item's paragraph child and the row is anchored there.

cases.name: blockquote-line-field-matches-once-via-nested-paragraph
cases.notes: §3.2 Containers: the quote's own text is `> `; the nested paragraph's `raw` starts at content (`spec/format` §1 inv. 7) and matches the line form → one row anchored to the paragraph. Unchanged by 1.1.

cases.name: blockquote-continuation-line-field-yields-nothing
cases.notes: §3.2: the nested paragraph's raw keeps the `> ` prefix on its continuation line, so the line form matches at neither level.

cases.name: nested-list-field-anchored-to-the-innermost-item
cases.notes: §3.2 Containers (1.1): the outer list, the outer item and the inner list all blank their children; the inner item's continuation line matches once.

cases.name: task-item-continuation-field
cases.notes: §3.2 (1.1): a continuation-line field of a task item is one row anchored to the task block (the list's own text is blank).

cases.name: bracketed-field-in-table-cell-anchored-to-the-row
cases.notes: §3.2 Containers (1.1): the table's own text is its delimiter row; the bracketed field belongs to the `table_row` that holds it → one scalar row.

cases.name: heading-bracketed-counts-line-form-does-not
cases.notes: §3.2: the bracketed form matches inside a heading's raw; `## job:: x` is defeated by the `#` marker. $title is the heading's visible text.

cases.name: key-shape
cases.notes: §3.2: `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` (case-insensitive): a leading underscore or digit, or a hyphen, disqualifies; CamelCase is fine.
cases.source:
# T

known_for2:: a

_bad:: b

2bad:: c

bad-key:: d

CamelCase:: e

cases.name: double-colon-in-value
cases.notes: §3.2 line form: the key is the first name, the value everything after — `b:: c`.

cases.name: bracketed-value-stops-at-first-closer
cases.notes: §3.2: `[^\]\n)]*?` — the value ends at the first `]` or `)`: "a (b".

cases.name: wikilink-shaped-field-matches
cases.notes: §3.2: the inner `[k:: v]` is a bracketed match (the outer `[` is skipped because `[` is not `[a-z]`).

cases.name: html-block-field-counts
cases.notes: §3.2: only code_fence blocks are skipped; an html_block's raw is scanned.
